newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sells 36,000 tonnes rice to Mauritius.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sells 36,000 tonnes rice to Mauritius.

text.p: Pakistan sold 36,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice to Mauritius, the state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan (TCP) said on Wednesday.
"Rice will be exported in four parcels till March 1998," Iftikhar Ahmed, chairman of the TCP told Reuters.

The first parcel of 12,000 tonnes at $235 per tonne FOB would be shipped in March/April, the second of 8,000 at $249 in May/June, the third of 8,000 at $249 in October/November and the fourth of 8,000 at $240 in March 1998, he said.
Exporter Khalid Ghori said the deal between the two governments had raised prices in the local market to $215/225 per tonne FOB.
Mauritius had also shown interest in Pakistan's superior quality basmati rice, Ghori said.
Ghori said IRRI-6 rice, which was being sold at between $205 and $210 per tonne FOB last week, was likely to rise further on foreign buying, including possible purchases by the Philippines.
He said private exporters had not been contacted by the Philippines but it might buy on a government-to-government level.
Ahmed said the Philippines had shown interest in buying Pakistani rice but it had not given any specific proposal.
A report from Manila said the Philippines' state-owned National Food Authority has signed a contract to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from Malaysia at $291.50 per tonnes C&F.
"Pakistan can sell to Philippines if it wants," Ahmed said.
